speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have any nightmares or bad dreams when you wake up frightened? Also, do you remember what happened when you wake up, or do you just feel scared?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she is not confused after waking and can be consoled, this points more toward nightmares rather than sleep terrors. Do you recall any specific stressors or fears, such as school pressure or changes at home, that might be contributing to these bad dreams?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do these frightened awakenings typically happen in the first half of the night or closer to morning, and have you noticed any snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Met all developmental milestones with no significant medical history. Social history: Attends school regularly, with usual playing habits and interactions with peers. Lives with both parents.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since she can recall the bad dreams and is not confused upon waking, these are classic nightmares rather than sleep terrors. I want to rule out obstructive sleep apnea as a contributing factor, so have you noticed any loud snoring or gasping for air during her sleep? REQUEST TEST: Polysomnography
